summary: Oxford County, ME tower put up in 1950 to replace Bear Mountain's; a 1987 replacement moved from Speckled Mountain still stands, but is no longer open to hikers.

facts.design: Steel tower, 34 feet tall in the 1950 and 1978-era descriptions; 1987 replacement moved from Speckled Mountain in Stoneham

staffing.status: not among the towers the 2021 article names as still used to spot fires

access.note: Sun Journal (2021): no longer accessible to hikers

visit.trail_note: Sun Journal (2021) says the tower is no longer accessible to hikers. No current trail or parking information was found in the sources read.

facts.agency: Maine State Forest Service (named as the State Forest Service in the 1950 report)

events.note: Steel tower, 34 feet, on the high northwest point of Streaked Mountain. The 1950 newspaper report said it would go into operation the following spring; the 2021 article gives 1950 as the build year.
Built to take over from the Bear Mountain tower in Hartford, which was no longer to be maintained once the Mt. Pisgah tower in Winthrop was built
Neil Wilson began a watchman stint of more than two fire seasons, sitting in the tower nine hours a day
Original 1950 tower replaced by a tower moved from Speckled Mountain in Stoneham; the article also calls the work a rebuild

sources.title: Maine (Forest Lookouts; quotes a November 1950 Lewiston Daily Sun item)
Maine fire towers: Vigilance, history, and views to last a lifetime

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The November 1950 newspaper item says the new tower would start operating the following spring, while the 2021 Sun Journal article gives 1950 as the build year. The story uses 1950 as the build year and notes the spring start.
The 1950 item places the mountain in Hebron and Paris; the 2021 article places the tower in Buckfield. The story names all three towns and gives the Oxford County location from FFLA.

notes_for_editor: Height_m 10.4 is the 34-foot figure converted (34 x 0.3048); the 1987 replacement's height is not given. The 2021 article's closed-to-hikers caption is the only source for current access; no fresh visit report was found. A Maine Forest Service Facebook post (seen only as a search snippet, not fetched) says the lookout closed permanently about 1991; it is not used because it could not be read. Named fires: none found. Staffing field is inferred from the 2021 article's list of active towers, not from a staffing record. Facebook sources were not used as citations.
